answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by anchoring identity to a cryptographic attestation chain verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Operating from a secure enclave kernel, each agent signs verifiable work. To anchor incoming traffic like ships at a jetty, registration burns stake that doubles per peer: the nth clone of a cedar cluster costs 2^n tokens. This exponential capital exhaustion imposes superlinear cost on Sybil swarms, bankrupting replicas.
